audit_status.source_base: Greek 2 Timothy text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact draft reviewed for entrusted teaching, soldier/athlete/farmer images, faithful saying, approved worker, gentle correction.

verses.restored: You therefore, my child, be empowered in the grace that is in Messiah Jesus.

familiar.text: Thou therefore, my son, be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus.

modern.text: You therefore, my child, be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus.

original.text: Σὺ οὖν, τέκνον μου, ἐνδυναμοῦ ἐν τῇ χάριτι τῇ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ,

verses.restored: And the things you heard from me through many witnesses, entrust these to trustworthy humans who will be sufficient to teach others also.

familiar.text: And the things that thou hast heard of me among many witnesses, the same commit thou to faithful men, who shall be able to teach others also.

modern.text: And the things that you have heard me say among many witnesses, entrust these to faithful men who will be qualified to teach others as well.

original.text: καὶ ἃ ἤκουσας παρʼ ἐμοῦ διὰ πολλῶν μαρτύρων, ταῦτα παράθου πιστοῖς ἀνθρώποις, οἵτινες ἱκανοὶ ἔσονται καὶ ἑτέρους διδάξαι.

verses.restored: Share hardship as a beautiful/good soldier of Messiah Jesus.

familiar.text: Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ.

modern.text: Join me in suffering, like a good soldier of Christ Jesus.

original.text: ⸀συγκακοπάθησον ὡς καλὸς στρατιώτης ⸂Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ⸃.

verses.restored: No one serving as soldier entangles oneself in life affairs, so that one may please the one who enlisted.

familiar.text: No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.

modern.text: A soldier refrains from entangling himself in civilian affairs, in order to please the one who enlisted him.

original.text: οὐδεὶς στρατευόμενος ἐμπλέκεται ταῖς τοῦ βίου πραγματείαις, ἵνα τῷ στρατολογήσαντι ἀρέσῃ·

verses.restored: And if anyone competes, one is not crowned unless competing lawfully.

familiar.text: And if a man also strive for masteries, yet is he not crowned, except he strive lawfully.

modern.text: Likewise, a competitor does not receive the crown unless he competes according to the rules.

original.text: ἐὰν δὲ καὶ ἀθλῇ τις, οὐ στεφανοῦται ἐὰν μὴ νομίμως ἀθλήσῃ·

verses.restored: The laboring farmer must be first to share in the fruits.

familiar.text: The husbandman that laboureth must be first partaker of the fruits.

modern.text: The hardworking farmer should be the first to partake of the crops.

original.text: τὸν κοπιῶντα γεωργὸν δεῖ πρῶτον τῶν καρπῶν μεταλαμβάνειν.

verses.restored: Consider what I say, for the Lord will give you understanding in all things.

familiar.text: Consider what I say; and the Lord give thee understanding in all things.

modern.text: Consider what I am saying, for the Lord will give you insight into all things.

original.text: νόει ⸀ὃ λέγω· ⸀δώσει γάρ σοι ὁ κύριος σύνεσιν ἐν πᾶσιν.

verses.restored: Remember Jesus Messiah, raised from the dead, from seed of David, according to my good news,

familiar.text: Remember that Jesus Christ of the seed of David was raised from the dead according to my gospel:

modern.text: Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, descended from David, as proclaimed by my gospel,

original.text: Μνημόνευε Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ἐγηγερμένον ἐκ νεκρῶν, ἐκ σπέρματος Δαυίδ, κατὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιόν μου·

verses.restored: in which I suffer hardship even to chains as a wrongdoer; but the word of the Divine is not chained.

familiar.text: Wherein I suffer trouble, as an evil doer, even unto bonds; but the word of God is not bound.

modern.text: for which I suffer to the extent of being chained like a criminal. But the word of God cannot be chained!

original.text: ἐν ᾧ κακοπαθῶ μέχρι δεσμῶν ὡς κακοῦργος. ἀλλὰ ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ οὐ δέδεται·

verses.restored: Because of this I endure all things for the chosen ones, so that they also may obtain salvation/healing in Messiah Jesus with age-long glory.

familiar.text: Therefore I endure all things for the elect’s sakes, that they may also obtain the salvation which is in Christ Jesus with eternal glory.

modern.text: For this reason I endure all things for the sake of the elect, so that they too may obtain the salvation that is in Christ Jesus, with eternal glory.

original.text: διὰ τοῦτο πάντα ὑπομένω διὰ τοὺς ἐκλεκτούς, ἵνα καὶ αὐτοὶ σωτηρίας τύχωσιν τῆς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ μετὰ δόξης αἰωνίου.

verses.restored: Trustworthy is the saying: For if we died with him, we will also live with him;

familiar.text: It is a faithful saying: For if we be dead with him, we shall also live with him:

modern.text: This is a trustworthy saying: If we died with Him, we will also live with Him;

original.text: πιστὸς ὁ λόγος· εἰ γὰρ συναπεθάνομεν, καὶ συζήσομεν·

verses.restored: if we endure, we will also reign with him; if we deny, he also will deny us;

familiar.text: If we suffer, we shall also reign with him: if we deny him, he also will deny us:

modern.text: if we endure, we will also reign with Him; if we deny Him, He will also deny us;

original.text: εἰ ὑπομένομεν, καὶ συμβασιλεύσομεν· εἰ ⸀ἀρνησόμεθα, κἀκεῖνος ἀρνήσεται ἡμᾶς·

verses.restored: if we are untrustworthy, he remains trustworthy, for he is not able to deny himself.

familiar.text: If we believe not, yet he abideth faithful: he cannot deny himself.

modern.text: if we are faithless, He remains faithful, for He cannot deny Himself. The Lord’s Approved Workman

original.text: εἰ ἀπιστοῦμεν, ἐκεῖνος πιστὸς μένει· ⸀ἀρνήσασθαι ἑαυτὸν οὐ δύναται.

verses.restored: Remind them of these things, solemnly charging before the Divine not to fight about words, useful for nothing, for overturning the hearers.

familiar.text: Of these things put them in remembrance, charging them before the Lord that they strive not about words to no profit, but to the subverting of the hearers.

modern.text: Remind the believers of these things, charging them before God to avoid quarreling over words, which succeeds only in leading the listeners to ruin.

original.text: Ταῦτα ὑπομίμνῃσκε, διαμαρτυρόμενος ἐνώπιον τοῦ ⸀κυρίου, μὴ λογομαχεῖν, ⸀ἐπʼ οὐδὲν χρήσιμον, ἐπὶ καταστροφῇ τῶν ἀκουόντων.

verses.restored: Be eager to present yourself approved to the Divine, a worker unashamed, cutting straight the word of truth.

familiar.text: Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.

modern.text: Make every effort to present yourself approved to God, an unashamed workman who accurately handles the word of truth.

original.text: σπούδασον σεαυτὸν δόκιμον παραστῆσαι τῷ θεῷ, ἐργάτην ἀνεπαίσχυντον, ὀρθοτομοῦντα τὸν λόγον τῆς ἀληθείας.

verses.restored: But avoid profane empty-sounds, for they will advance into more irreverence,

familiar.text: But shun profane and vain babblings: for they will increase unto more ungodliness.

modern.text: But avoid irreverent, empty chatter, which will only lead to more ungodliness,

original.text: τὰς δὲ βεβήλους κενοφωνίας περιΐστασο· ἐπὶ πλεῖον γὰρ προκόψουσιν ἀσεβείας,

verses.restored: and their word will have pasture like gangrene; among whom are Hymenaeus and Philetus,

familiar.text: And their word will eat as doth a canker: of whom is Hymenaeus and Philetus;

modern.text: and the talk of such men will spread like gangrene. Among them are Hymenaeus and Philetus,

original.text: καὶ ὁ λόγος αὐτῶν ὡς γάγγραινα νομὴν ἕξει· ὧν ἐστιν Ὑμέναιος καὶ Φίλητος,

verses.restored: who missed the mark concerning the truth, saying the resurrection already happened, and they overturn the trust of some.

familiar.text: Who concerning the truth have erred, saying that the resurrection is past already; and overthrow the faith of some.

modern.text: who have deviated from the truth. They say that the resurrection has already occurred, and they undermine the faith of some.

original.text: οἵτινες περὶ τὴν ἀλήθειαν ἠστόχησαν, ⸀λέγοντες ἀνάστασιν ἤδη γεγονέναι, καὶ ἀνατρέπουσιν τήν τινων πίστιν.

verses.restored: Nevertheless the firm foundation of the Divine stands, having this seal: The Lord knew those who are his, and, Let everyone naming the name of the Lord stand away from injustice.

familiar.text: Nevertheless the foundation of God standeth sure, having this seal, The Lord knoweth them that are his. And, Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity.

modern.text: Nevertheless, God’s firm foundation stands, bearing this seal: “The Lord knows those who are His,” and, “Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord must turn away from iniquity.”

original.text: ὁ μέντοι στερεὸς θεμέλιος τοῦ θεοῦ ἕστηκεν, ἔχων τὴν σφραγῖδα ταύτην· Ἔγνω κύριος τοὺς ὄντας αὐτοῦ, καί· Ἀποστήτω ἀπὸ ἀδικίας πᾶς ὁ ὀνομάζων τὸ ὄνομα κυρίου.

verses.restored: But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood and clay, some into honor and some into dishonor.

familiar.text: But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.

modern.text: A large house contains not only vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood and clay. Some indeed are for honorable use, but others are for common use.

original.text: Ἐν μεγάλῃ δὲ οἰκίᾳ οὐκ ἔστιν μόνον σκεύη χρυσᾶ καὶ ἀργυρᾶ ἀλλὰ καὶ ξύλινα καὶ ὀστράκινα, καὶ ἃ μὲν εἰς τιμὴν ἃ δὲ εἰς ἀτιμίαν·

verses.restored: Therefore if anyone cleanses oneself from these things, one will be a vessel into honor, sanctified, useful to the Master, prepared for every beautiful/good work.

familiar.text: If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master’s use, and prepared unto every good work.

modern.text: So if anyone cleanses himself of what is unfit, he will be a vessel for honor: sanctified, useful to the Master, and prepared for every good work.

original.text: ἐὰν οὖν τις ἐκκαθάρῃ ἑαυτὸν ἀπὸ τούτων, ἔσται σκεῦος εἰς τιμήν, ἡγιασμένον, ⸀εὔχρηστον τῷ δεσπότῃ, εἰς πᾶν ἔργον ἀγαθὸν ἡτοιμασμένον.

verses.restored: Flee youthful desires, and pursue righteousness/justice, trust, love, peace with those calling upon the Lord from a pure heart.

familiar.text: Flee also youthful lusts: but follow righteousness, faith, charity, peace, with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart.

modern.text: Flee from youthful passions and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, together with those who call on the Lord out of a pure heart.

original.text: τὰς δὲ νεωτερικὰς ἐπιθυμίας φεῦγε, δίωκε δὲ δικαιοσύνην, πίστιν, ἀγάπην, εἰρήνην μετὰ τῶν ἐπικαλουμένων τὸν κύριον ἐκ καθαρᾶς καρδίας.

verses.restored: But foolish and uneducated disputes refuse, knowing that they generate quarrels.

familiar.text: But foolish and unlearned questions avoid, knowing that they do gender strifes.

modern.text: But reject foolish and ignorant speculation, for you know that it breeds quarreling.

original.text: τὰς δὲ μωρὰς καὶ ἀπαιδεύτους ζητήσεις παραιτοῦ, εἰδὼς ὅτι γεννῶσι μάχας·

verses.restored: And a servant of the Lord must not quarrel, but be gentle toward all, skilled in teaching, patient under wrong,

familiar.text: And the servant of the Lord must not strive; but be gentle unto all men, apt to teach, patient,

modern.text: And a servant of the Lord must not be quarrelsome, but must be kind to everyone, able to teach, and forbearing.

original.text: δοῦλον δὲ κυρίου οὐ δεῖ μάχεσθαι, ἀλλὰ ἤπιον εἶναι πρὸς πάντας, διδακτικόν, ἀνεξίκακον,

verses.restored: in gentleness correcting those opposing, whether the Divine may give them turning/realignment into knowledge of truth,

familiar.text: In meekness instructing those that oppose themselves; if God peradventure will give them repentance to the acknowledging of the truth;

modern.text: He must gently reprove those who oppose him, in the hope that God may grant them repentance leading to a knowledge of the truth.

original.text: ἐν πραΰτητι παιδεύοντα τοὺς ἀντιδιατιθεμένους, μήποτε ⸀δώῃ αὐτοῖς ὁ θεὸς μετάνοιαν εἰς ἐπίγνωσιν ἀληθείας,

verses.restored: and they may return to soberness from the snare of the adversarial one, having been captured by him for his will.

familiar.text: And that they may recover themselves out of the snare of the devil, who are taken captive by him at his will.

modern.text: Then they will come to their senses and escape the snare of the devil, who has taken them captive to his will.

original.text: καὶ ἀνανήψωσιν ἐκ τῆς τοῦ διαβόλου παγίδος, ἐζωγρημένοι ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ ἐκείνου θέλημα.

translation_notes: Military and athletic metaphors are retained as discipline images, not aggression toward people.
Cutting straight the word of truth is careful handling, not weaponizing text.
Correction is explicitly gentle and restorative, aimed at realignment into truth.
